title: Swap Success Across Sixteen Templates
takeaway: One J-lens vector, swapped identically into sixteen different function contexts, redirects the model's top answer on 76 of 192 trials, and on 101 of 192 when the swap is applied at double strength. Failures concentrate where the source concept was only weakly loaded in the workspace before any intervention, so workspace loading predicts whether the swap lands. Together the two panels are the paper's quantitative case that a single shared representation is read by many downstream computations.
walkthrough:
This figure is the quantitative summary of the [[flexible-generalization]] experiment; in the article it renders as a live widget rather than a static image. The setup comes from the surrounding section. Prompts such as "the capital of France is" apply a function to an argument. A [[lens-coordinate-swap]] exchanges the argument's [[j-lens-vector]] for another from the same category, France for China, applied identically at every token position across a band of middle layers, regardless of which prompt it lands in. If that vector is a broadcast representation, each downstream circuit should read the swapped-in vector and answer for the new argument.

The left panel gives one entry per function template, sixteen in all: four templates for each of four argument categories under the [[function-template-protocol]] — countries, months, animals, and number words. Each category has four arguments. Each argument can be swapped for any of the other three, so a template contributes $4 \times 3 = 12$ source-target pairs, and sixteen templates give $16 \times 12 = 192$ trials. The plotted value is the fraction of a template's 12 pairs whose target-appropriate answer becomes the model's top-1 output token. A filled circle marks this fraction at normal swap strength; a cross marks it at double strength, $\alpha = 2$, where the source vector is subtracted and the target added at twice the magnitude ([[swap-strength-alpha]]). The aggregate over all templates is 76 of 192 successes at $\alpha = 1$ and 101 of 192 at $\alpha = 2$.

The right panel plots, per trial, the magnitude of the swap's effect at shifting the model's output toward the target answer against the source argument's [[workspace-loading]]: the [[cosine-similarity]] between the [[residual-stream]] and that concept's lens vector, averaged over the argument and readout positions of an unmodified forward pass. Loading predicts success. Country arguments load highest and swap most reliably; in the appendix's per-trial grids, 42 of 48 country cells reach rank 1, while number relations reach 0 of 48 at $\alpha = 1$. The paper offers two readings of the number-word failure: the model may compute over small integers outside the workspace, or its working representation of them may simply not align with the number tokens' lens vectors — an instance of the lens's [[single-token-limitation]]. The evidence does not decide between the two.

terms.definition: A prompt frame that applies one fixed operation to a slotted argument, such as "the capital of ___ is". The experiment uses sixteen of them, four per argument category.

An ordered (source, target) choice of two arguments from the same category: the source sits in the prompt and the target's lens vector is swapped in. Four arguments per category yield twelve such pairs per template.
The intervention scored here: the activation's coordinates along the source and target J-lens vectors are read, exchanged, and written back, at every token position across a band of middle layers.
The left panel's marker for a template's success fraction at normal swap strength ($\alpha = 1$); these fractions sum to 76 successes out of 192 trials.
The left panel's marker for the same template's success fraction when the swap is applied at double strength; these sum to 101 out of 192.
A multiplier on the swap's magnitude. At $\alpha = 2$ the source lens vector is subtracted, and the target added, at twice the normal strength.
The answer the template implies for the swapped-in argument — China's capital rather than France's. A trial succeeds when this token becomes the model's single most likely next token.
The most probable token in the model's output distribution. The left panel's success criterion is the target answer reaching this position.
The left panel's plotted quantity: of a template's twelve trials, the share whose target answer reaches top-1.

The right panel's horizontal quantity: the cosine similarity between the residual stream and the source concept's lens vector, averaged over the argument and readout positions of an unmodified forward pass. It measures how strongly the concept was in the workspace before any intervention.
The right panel's vertical quantity: how far the swap shifts the model's output distribution toward the target answer, plotted per trial.
The four argument categories, four templates each. They span a range of swap reliability: countries swap best, number words worst.
The argument actually written in the prompt, whose lens vector the swap removes.
The direction in residual-stream space associated with one vocabulary token by the Jacobian lens; the object the swap exchanges between source and target.

numbers.meaning: Function templates in the experiment: four argument categories (countries, months, animals, number words) times four functions per category.
Both the number of functions per category and the number of arguments per category; the two fours are independent design choices.
Source-target swap pairs per template: each of 4 arguments can be swapped for any of the other 3, giving 4 × 3 = 12 ordered pairs.
Total swap trials: 16 templates × 12 pairs. The denominator for both aggregate counts.
Trials at normal strength ($\alpha = 1$) on which the target answer reaches top-1 — roughly 40%. The filled circles in the left panel decompose this by template.

Successes when the swap strength is doubled — roughly 53%. The gain over 76 supports the paper's reading that failed $\alpha = 1$ swaps often move the activation in the right direction but not far enough.
The double-strength condition: the source vector is subtracted and the target added at twice the normal magnitude.
From the appendix's per-trial grids: off-diagonal country cells whose target answer reaches rank 1 at α = 1. Countries are the best-loaded and most swappable category.

Number-relation swaps that succeed at α = 1 — none. Number words have the lowest workspace loading, and the paper leaves open whether small-integer computation bypasses the workspace or merely misaligns with the number tokens' lens vectors.
